label: Institution
name: Bank of India
summary:
Bank of India is one of India's largest public sector banks, founded in 1906 in Mumbai (then Bombay) by a group of eminent businessmen led by Sir Sassoon J. David. As a state-owned bank following nationalization in 1969, Bank of India is part of India's public banking system that serves as the primary financial infrastructure for millions of Indians, particularly in rural and semi-urban areas where private banks do not operate profitably.

The 1969 nationalization of India's 14 major banks by Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was one of independent India's most consequential economic policy decisions, transforming banking from a private sector activity to a government tool for directing credit to agriculture, small industries, and underserved populations. Bank of India, along with the State Bank of India and other nationalized banks, became instruments of the government's 'priority sector lending' requirements.

Bank of India's international network includes branches in 22 countries spanning London, New York, Tokyo, Singapore, and East Africa — reflecting India's diaspora and trade connections. The bank's 5,000+ domestic branches serve approximately 70 million customers. India's public banking system has faced recurring challenges: the 2015-2020 non-performing asset (NPA) crisis left Bank of India with 15%+ gross NPA ratios, requiring capital injections from the Indian government and creating pressure for privatization.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Bank of India's nationalization under Indira Gandhi made it an instrument of India's development banking model — extending credit to agriculture and underserved populations as part of socialist economic planning.
